events.title: Argentina Declares Independence
events.description: The Congress of Tucumán formally declared the independence of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata (modern Argentina) from Spain, issuing the declaration in San Miguel de Tucumán.
events.significance: Marked the formal break from Spanish colonial rule and is celebrated annually as Argentina's Independence Day.

events.title: Death of President Zachary Taylor
events.description: Zachary Taylor, the 12th President of the United States, died in office after about 16 months in the presidency, following a sudden illness that began after attending Fourth of July festivities. Vice President Millard Fillmore succeeded him.
events.significance: Fillmore's succession shifted federal policy and helped pave the way for the Compromise of 1850, which temporarily eased tensions between free and slave states.

events.title: Fourteenth Amendment Ratified
events.description: The Fourteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified when the required three-fourths of the states approved it, granting citizenship to all persons born or naturalized in the United States and guaranteeing equal protection under the law.
events.significance: It became one of the most important constitutional amendments, forming the basis for landmark civil rights rulings such as Brown v. Board of Education.

events.title: First Wimbledon Championships Begin
events.description: The first Wimbledon lawn tennis championship started at the All England Croquet and Lawn Tennis Club in London, with the men's singles competition won by Spencer Gore.
events.significance: Wimbledon became the oldest and one of the most prestigious tennis tournaments in the world.

events.title: South Sudan Becomes Independent
events.description: South Sudan declared independence from Sudan, following a January 2011 referendum in which nearly 99 percent of voters chose secession, ending decades of civil war.
events.significance: It became the world's newest sovereign nation and was admitted to the United Nations shortly after, though it later faced serious internal conflict.
